# Results -- Study 300 (Sports-Sentiment) on the single-country ETF tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Elimination losses are
hardcoded in [`data.py`](../sports_sentiment/data.py) (60 events, 1998-2024). Next-day
returns are the close-to-close simple return of the first trading session strictly
after each match (one-day execution lag), from iShares single-country ETFs + ^GSPC
daily closes (PRICE-only, USD), cached per-ticker under `_cache/`. Match the
fingerprint below to confirm you hold the same data. As-of **2026-06-18**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n events | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| iShares single-country ETFs + ^GSPC (daily close, price-only, USD) | response dates 1998-07-01 to 2024-07-15 | 59 (of 60; EWZ pre-2000 drops Brazil's 1998 final) | `95d210fa8556` |
| Elimination-loss table | World Cup / Euro / Copa knockout losses 1998-2024 | 60 events | hardcoded constant |

## The headline test -- next-day return after a national-team loss

The Edmans, Garcia & Norli (2007) hypothesis: the mean next-day return should be
significantly **negative**, of order **-49 bps**. On the tradable ETF tape:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Mean next-day return | **+33.46 bps** |
| Newey-West HAC t (H0: mean = 0, 1 lag) | **+1.606** |
| Plain i.i.d. t | +1.633 |
| Bootstrap P(mean >= 0), one-sided | 0.955 |
| Down days | 26 / 59 (44.1%) |

The sign is **wrong** (positive, not negative) and the HAC t is **+1.6** -- short
of significance in *either* direction, and on the opposite side of zero from the
hypothesis. The desk bar for a REAL stamp is **HAC t <= -2 with a negative mean**;
this fails on both counts. The minimum detectable mean at |t|=2 with ~120 bps daily
vol and n=59 is ~31 bps, so even a -49 bps effect would be borderline here -- but
the observed mean is the wrong sign entirely.

## Sub-group cuts (HAC t, 1 lag)

| Group | n | mean (bps) | HAC t | frac. down |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| All eliminations | 59 | +33.46 | +1.606 | 44.1% |
| Penalty-shootout losses | 18 | **-14.48** | -0.484 | 44.4% |
| Non-shootout losses | 41 | +54.51 | +2.147 | 43.9% |
| World Cup only | 33 | +12.13 | +0.532 | 42.4% |
| Euro / Copa | 26 | +60.54 | +1.676 | 46.2% |

Only the **penalty-shootout** sub-group (the most painful losses, where Edmans
finds the effect strongest) is negative in *sign* (-14 bps) -- but with n=18 and
HAC t = -0.48 it is indistinguishable from noise. The non-shootout group is
*positive and nominally significant* (+2.15), which, with no economic rationale for
a positive mood effect after a loss, reads as a multiple-testing artifact rather
than a finding.

## Could you trade it?

The natural trade is to short the country ETF for the single next session after
each loss. PnL per event = `-(next-day return)`; round-trip cost = 2 x one-way
(shorts also pay borrow; single-country ETFs are wide).

| One-way cost (bps) | Gross mean (bps) | Net mean (bps) | Net hit-rate |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 | -33.46 | -33.46 | ~39% |
| 5 | -33.46 | **-43.46** | 39.0% |
| 10 | -33.46 | -53.46 | ~39% |

The short **loses money even before costs**, because the market drifted up after
these losses in our sample. Costs deepen the loss. The strategy is also idle ~99%
of the time (events cluster in six-week tournament windows every two years) -- a
capacity/utilisation problem on top of a negative edge.

## Positive control (synthetic)

Planting a -49 bps loss effect in a synthetic panel and sweeping n:

| n events | planted-effect HAC t | null HAC t |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 60 | ~ -3.4 | ~ +0.5 |
| 150 | ~ -5 | ~ 0 |
| 300 | ~ -7.4 | ~ +0.5 |
| 600 | ~ -10 | ~ 0 |

The engine drives the HAC t strongly negative when a -49 bps effect is real, and
keeps the null near zero. The real-tape **+1.6** is therefore a statement about the
**tradable proxy and sample**, not a broken test.

## Honesty checks

- **Execution lag:** one trading day -- the match is an evening event, so the full
  next session is the tradable window (close-to-close).
- **Costs:** one-way x NAV, doubled for the round trip; shorts pay borrow. Net
  numbers labeled separately from gross.
- **Returns:** PRICE-only (ETF/index price, no dividends), USD -- labeled.
- **Survivorship:** ETFs are live single-country funds (no dead-fund bias), but the
  basket and currency differ from Edmans's local-index measurement -- a proxy
  mismatch, not survivorship in the classic sense.
- **Multiple testing:** the one nominally-significant sub-group (non-shootout,
  +2.15) is positive with no economic rationale and is treated as noise.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** The Edmans loss effect is a genuine, much-cited behavioural
  finding (so this is not folklore), but on the investable single-country ETF tape
  the mean next-day return is **+33 bps** with HAC t = **+1.6** -- wrong sign, not
  significant. Literature support without a confirming real-tape t-stat earns WEAK,
  not Real, by the desk rubric.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** Shorting on loss nets **-43 bps/event**, is idle 99% of
  the time, and pays wide single-country-ETF spreads and borrow. There is no
  tradable edge on this tape.
